newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan accuses ICRC of transporting rebels, arms.
newsitem.headline: Sudan accuses ICRC of transporting rebels, arms.

text.p: Sudan accused the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) of helping rebels fighting the Khartoum government and said on Wednesday it has stopped all activities of the relief group inside its borders.
State radio said the decision was effective from Tuesday. It quoted a Sudan Ministry of Social Planning statement accusing the ICRC of "violating humanitarian principles and its own mandate."
There was no immediate ICRC comment.
State radio said the ICRC was transporting rebels loyal to the Sudan Peoples Liberation Army (SPLA) headed by John Garang as well as carrying weapons and ammunition for the group.
A pro-government southern group had also detained two ICRC workers as well as an Australian nurse, the state's Humanitarian Assistance Commission said in a statement.
The commission said an ICRC plane landed on Friday at Wunrok, more than 800 km (500 miles) south of Khartoum, and was met by Carubino Kwanyin Bol's group.
"When the plane was unloading, the crew and passengers of the plane were surprised to find out that they had been received by forces loyal to Carubino and not Garang," it said.
Bol heads a splinter group of the mainstream SPLA fighting for the past 13 years the Islamist government for autonomy of the mainly Christian and animist south.
He has signed a peace deal with the Khartoum government and the statement said his forces were holding the plane's Canadian pilot and its Kenyan co-pilot and the nurse.
Five SPLA soldiers and boxes of ammuntion were also captured, it added.
